maya: Heads up — nightly eval for quantized-13B (summarization bench) flipped again, rouge-L down ~1.3 vs yesterday. Same commit, same prompts. Suspect nondet sampling vs seed handling. Anyone tracking? :eyes:
Jin: saw that too. numbers bounce between runs. top_p set to 0.92 and temp=0.0 (we use nucleus sampling for beam fallback), so odd it's nondet.
Taylor: temp=0.0 + top_p should be deterministic in theory, but our runner does a mixed path: if top_p<1 it calls sampler.multinomial that uses worker RNG state.
Sam: Confirmed — worker pool seeds only on worker spin-up. We don't reseed per request. If a worker handles multiple requests in a batch, ordering can change RNG consumption.
Leo: Another angle: quantized kernels use fp16 logits + softmax; tiny FP differences + unordered tie-breaking can make top_p selection diverge. For top_p you depend on sorted cumulative probs; equal probs tie-breaker currently uses dict iteration order.
maya: Oof. So two failure modes: (1) RNG stream reuse across requests (seed scope), (2) nondet tie-breaker / float jitter in quantized path. Both could explain run-to-run metric variance.
Jin: Quick repro idea: force single worker, run same eval twice with fixed EVAL_SEED and dump the sampled token IDs. If those differ, it's seed/RNG. If identical there, maybe float ordering.
Taylor: Repro snippet I used locally:
```bash
EVAL_SEED=42 python eval_runner.py --model quant-13b --workers=1 --top_p=0.92 --dump-samples out1.json
EVAL_SEED=42 python eval_runner.py --model quant-13b --workers=1 --top_p=0.92 --dump-samples out2.json
diff out1.json out2.json || echo "deterministic"
```
Sam: Running that now on my laptop. initial result: out1 vs out2 differ. Looks like same seed but different per-inference time values -> worker RNG state mutated by background health checks?
Taylor: Are we using global random.Random vs per-request np.random or torch.Generator? We should centralize to a per-request generator object derived from seed.
Leo: Also, on the quantized code path we do an inplace softmax reduction that depends on thread scheduling — not safe. I'll add a stable sort on (prob, idx) before cumulative sum to canonicalize top_p selection.
maya: Two parallel fixes then: reseed-per-request + canonical top_p tie-breaker + avoid inplace non-deterministic reductions in quantized kernels.
Jin: I'll write a small unit test in eval-runner-tests that runs 20 repeats of the same mini-batch and asserts identical sampled token sequences when EVAL_SEED fixed and workers=1.
Taylor: I'll open PR: "runner: per-request Generator from EVAL_SEED; stable-top_p-sorting". Includes repro harness and a note about fp16 nondet.
Sam: CI note — nightly uses --workers=4. Even if we fix single-worker determinism we need to ensure multi-worker reproducibility for evals. Plan: CI can run determinism canary with --workers=1 and --workers=4, and we assert deterministic summary stats within epsilon.
ci-bot: Nightly job 1812345600 reported flaky metrics (variance > threshold). Marking job for retest.
Leo: Quick patch idea for top_p deterministic selection:
```py
# before: sorted_probs = probs.sort(descending=True)
# after: pairs = list(enumerate(probs))
#        pairs.sort(key=lambda (i,p): (-p, i))  # stable tie-break by index
#        cum = np.cumsum([p for _,p in pairs])
```
Taylor: Good. Also switch to float32 accumulation when computing cumulative sum even if logits are fp16: cast to float32, compute cumsum, then back to fp16 mask. Cuts jitter.
maya: Timeline? This is causing noisy eval alerts and wasting time triaging.
Taylor: I'll PR now. Estimated review + CI run ~ 4 hours. The unit test Jin adds will block merging until green.
Jin: After PR lands, I'll schedule a backfill of the last 5 nightly evals on fixed commit to confirm the regression disappears.
Sam: Also add a temporary flag EVAL_FORCE_DETERMINISTIC that the CI can enable to gate rollouts until we fully fix quant kernels.
maya: thanks team. appreciate the quick triage. :pray:
Taylor: opening PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-runner/pull/212
Jin: tagging QE + release-notes for the change.
ci-bot: PR 212 CI started — job/runner-unit-tests (expected 30m).
